title: fix(codex): keep session catalog queries in memory
body:
Related: #150112, #150514, #150196

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes slow sidebar catalog polling when unchanged Codex histories repeatedly trigger native discovery and preview parsing.

## User Impact

Catalog pages, cwd filters, and title searches use resident display rows while the home fits in memory. Native events keep Gateway-driven threads current; archive acknowledgements hide rows immediately. Ephemeral helpers are excluded, Codex's selected rollout remains authoritative, and open sources retain their live activity/settings even when cached rows are evicted.

The 20,000-row retention cap does not limit discovery. Saturated searches and older pages use bounded native database-only requests, which can be slower and perform foreground projection. Cold startup uses a bounded first-page wait with existing continuation/retry responses; saved SQLite rows remain available during reconciliation. The wire contract and sidebar polling cadence are unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

One index per Codex home replaces per-query TTL/head-page producers. Reconstructible display rows use OpenClaw's SQLite plugin state, C2's 500-character preview bound and prefix selector, and tie-safe pagination. Native metadata owns displayed fields and selected paths. Notifications, database-only metadata walks, and a streamed 30-second day-folder stat scan maintain currency; only changed rollouts receive bounded reads.

A foreground fallback request shares one **20-native-read budget and deadline** across title search, exclusion filling, scheduler steps, and nested metadata/membership/descendant reads. It retains one 64-row page at a time and preserves directional continuation. Source health settles once for the complete fallback outcome; closing abandons its probe. Background hydration keeps its separate grouped attempt and budget. Overflow uses the same live settings/status owners before filtering; remote exact access always verifies fresh non-archived membership, including resident hits. Node lookup no longer treats 100 pages as absence.

Gateway aggregation coalesces concurrent operations only and uses #150196's resident session-row projection. Current binding/state authority checks remain. Progress retains one latest one-host frame per selected catalog/host and one preparation job per subscriber; memory scales with distinct selected pairs. Retirement clears queued frames and joins admitted work. Generic admission/lifetime handling remains for providers, remote transport, progress, and shutdown.

**Zero I/O applies only to local queries answered entirely from resident rows.** Saturation discovery, exact actions, remote enumeration, and Gateway authority checks are outside that claim. Native thread/list has no bounded response projection: the catalog discards unused fields and detaches bounded metadata after decode, but full wire JSON still creates transient allocations.

No new configuration, sidecar, table, or schema version is introduced. Admission and restoration cap each home at 20,000 rows, evicting archived-oldest first. Fields, paths, queues, fingerprints, and cursor history are bounded; strings are detached. Realistic row JSON measures 214,561 bytes at 490 rows and 8,880,042 bytes at 20,000 rows.

| Maximum admitted UTF-16 text payload per home | 490 current rows | 20,000 current rows |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Rows only | 12,219,620 B | 498,760,000 B |
| Settled rows plus independently full field/path indexes | 495,100,132 B | 981,640,512 B |
| Conservative active-owner inventory, charging all independent caps together | 4,483,373,422 B | 4,969,913,802 B |

Capacity charges two bytes per UTF-16 unit. The active inventory overcounts phases that normally cannot peak together and includes old row generations, pending persistence/projection work, paths, cursors, and cleanup keys. Ancillary collections can remain at 20,000 entries with only 490 current rows. Object/allocator overhead, native/caller buffers, pre-admission callbacks, provenance caches, generic SQLite predecode, and Gateway progress frames are excluded. **This is not a total heap/RSS ceiling.**

## Evidence

**Current landing CI:** [Exact-head run 35286681006](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35286681006) completed successfully for `28dbe04fd14e98c48c59b53f02b101cbb26921b8`. The earlier observation below is historical.

<details>
<summary>Earlier voice-call teardown observation</summary>

Published head `28dbe04fd14e98c48c59b53f02b101cbb26921b8` is OPEN, ready, and MERGEABLE; the worktree is clean and synced. **Exact-head CI is blocked by [voice-call shard teardown in job 105420675832](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35286681006/job/105420675832)** (`checks-node-changed-extensions-bundle-33`). All 165 tests in its 15 files passed, then Vitest reported one unhandled teardown error: `[vitest-pool-runner]: Timeout waiting for worker to respond`. No test assertion failed and no specific test is attributed. The exact-head rollup failed and the bounded watch exited 15; the overall run was still `in_progress` at the last read, so no final run conclusion is claimed.

</details>

This is an untouched voice-call owner teardown blocker: none of the 15 shard files or other voice-call files changed in this branch. The database-worker list only adds six Codex paths and changes no runner runtime. Cause and flakiness are not established. No retry, timing change, assertion weakening, or merge followed the failure.

The previous timeout-forwarding regression is fixed in `28dbe04fd14e98c48c59b53f02b101cbb26921b8`. Undefined timeout remains undefined outside foreground scope, while scoped reads retain their remaining deadline. Tests were unchanged: valid red reproduced one failure / 13 passed; the corrected run passes **253 tests in 21 files**, scoped P2 review and the full changed-file check pass, and [the original bundle-31 job now succeeds](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/35286681006/job/105420675756). The same-repository PR still reports `maintainerCanModify: false`; both authorized enabling attempts were rejected by tooling input protection, with no bypass or setting-success claim.

Current U/V proof passes **240 tests in 21 files**: 239 regression tests in 20 files plus a disjoint composed benchmark. All seven new regressions pass after the final test-declaration cleanup. The earlier focused 61-test run overlaps and is not added. Valid red proof reproduced four failures: 400 native reads against a 20-read limit in inline/stepped filling, and six calls rather than four when a later page failed. The completed fixes preserve assertions, budgets, and background hydration ownership.

Earlier meaningful regressions cover ephemeral helpers and restart, selected paths, native metadata and live activity, cold navigation, bounded restoration, exact membership, and independent host progress. Archive and Gateway-selection fixture gaps found by CI were corrected through their real membership/readiness contracts. Earlier upstream guard failures were incorporated from main. No failed hosted job was rerun; detailed history and retained logs remain in the lane report.

A broader historical run passed **908 tests and timed out once across 79 files**. The native-allocation fixture exceeded its unchanged 120,000 ms limit and was reported at 124,751 ms. It was not rerun, skipped, or given a larger budget. Its earlier successful measurements are retained below as historical evidence.

The local query measurement is refreshed from the now-committed timeout-forwarding repair. The composed result remains the prior U/V measurement; it was not rerun and is not presented as a new timing for this repair. The local fixture mocks native latency and measures 100 warm lists across the former TTL boundary. Neither fixture measures saturation fallback latency or CPU. Cold/native-walk measurements below are older and labeled separately.

| Measurement | Before | Resident |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| List p50 | 0.106 ms | 0.123917 ms |
| List p95 | 2.064 ms | 0.201000 ms |
| `thread/list` calls per 100 lists | 109 | 0 |
| Main-thread CPU per list | 0.319 ms | 0.157890 ms |

The composed fixture uses the actual Gateway handler, public plugin registration, real SQLite stores, 3,000 native rows, 3,000 local rows, and three actual Continue adoptions. A synthetic loopback endpoint supplies hydration. Four warmed head/search/opaque-cursor variants precede 100 measured lists; startup calibration confirms the counters see the real paths.

| Composed warm request measurement | Result |
| --- | ---: |
| p50 / p95 | 7.060042 / 67.805084 ms |
| Main-thread CPU per list | 7.05727 ms |
| Native RPCs / filesystem read-open calls / plugin-worker operations per list | 0 / 0 / 0 |
| Total explicit SQLite read statements per list | 20 |
| Global SQLite freshness / native binding authority / other SQL reads per list | 3 / 3 / 14 |
| Session-entry table SQL reads per list | 0 |
| Session payload SQL reads per list | 0 |
| Sampled allocations per list, separate instrumented pass | 5,602,052.48 B |
| Preview / terminal-sanitizer self-samples, separate 710-sample CPU profile | 0 / 0 |

Median meets the 20 ms goal. The observed **67.805084 ms p95 is higher** than the prior pre-U/V 15.038833 ms result; no cause is inferred and the earlier value is not substituted. Global SQLite freshness counts state-database checks, not session-entry cache reads. The other-SQL bucket is not fully classified. Non-admin visibility retains its canonical profile-count authority read; administrators bypass that irrelevant query. Counters measure API calls/statements rather than disk access; sampling can miss calls shorter than its interval. No authority cache was added to force zero SQL.

The **historical native comparison** uses 3,000 threads, 64 KiB first-user previews, 199,026,000 rollout bytes, and 47 database-only pages, with the same prepared-preview map in both modes. It measures the retained-response boundary, not current-head or foreground-list latency. The later timed-out run produced no replacement measurements.

| Instrumented native walk | Ordinary response | Catalog boundary |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Retained 64-row page JSON | 4,278,468 B | 75,972 B |
| Retained-page heap delta after GC | 4,254,496 B | -296,232 B |
| Post-walk heap delta after GC | -217,848 B | 47,688 B |
| Sampled walk allocations | 602,581,440 B | 615,272,248 B |
| Sampled peak heap growth | 45,556,480 B | 76,210,880 B |
| Sampled peak RSS growth | 88,457,216 B | 112,738,304 B |
| Instrumented walk elapsed | 4,983.840 ms | 4,355.072 ms |

Signed heap deltas include GC noise; negative values are not negative retained memory. Peaks were sampled at page boundaries. **Retained responses shrink, but total allocations and RSS peaks are not shown lower.** Removing wire/JSON allocation requires an upstream bounded projection.

The **historical cold fixture** contains 490 rollouts totaling 267,304,800 bytes. Native initialization took **12.607327 seconds**. First data—64 rows and a cursor—arrived **2.263123 seconds after list start**, or **14.881307 seconds since launch**. All rows and the completion marker were durable **17.877998 seconds since launch**: eight pages and 5.259816 seconds hydration. SQLite restart returned 64 rows in **498.922458 ms**, with zero native list calls. Initialization is the largest measured component; no cause for timing variation is inferred. Test-runner compilation is excluded.

No production deployment or post-deployment CPU profile is claimed. The docs cover hydration, currency, overflow, bounds, and remaining I/O.

Writer ownership clears before promise settlement, and draining joins following writes. The free snapshot export is removed; capacity regressions use the real persistence owner. |

This affects external fallback freshness; failure is retryable and preserves existing rows. Native Gateway-driven metadata remains authoritative. |

Unchanged assertions pass in 253 tests / 21 files, and scoped review is clean. Committed, full checks pass, and the corresponding hosted bundle-31 job succeeds. |

</details>

## Follow-ups

- External-origin fallback can miss JSONL records crossing sampled boundaries or first-user content outside the bounded prefix/tail. Gateway-driven metadata, live settings, and turn-start recency come from native observations. Existing rows keep their known preview when sampling misses it; a new immutable external rollout without a sampled preview can remain undiscovered until it changes.
- A capped Zstd prefix can fail before reaching the decoded-output limit for some valid low-compression streams. Failures remain retryable and preserve existing rows; complete-record and compressed-tail fallback freshness remain separate work.
- A nonempty raw preview consisting only of whitespace/control text may be sanitized again by background walks after its bounded display preview becomes empty. Queries served entirely from resident rows do no preview derivation; saturation fallback can project newly fetched native rows on the foreground path.
- Native wire responses still include full previews. Eliminating their transient JSON allocation requires an upstream bounded projection; the retained-response reduction does not establish that all process RSS bursts are eliminated.
- The generic plugin-state `entries()` API decodes a complete namespace before extension validation. Resident admission limits bound retained catalog data, not that generic predecode peak for abnormal stored values. The generic one-MiB value allowance permits 19.532 GiB serialized across 20,001 abnormal entries before validation. Normal catalog writes contain only bounded row metadata; a paged generic state reader is separate work.


### Maintainer landing applicability

The maintainer ruling at 00:28Z classifies this as a reconstructible cache over the existing `PluginStateKeyedStore` SDK contract, stored under a new namespace. It changes no schema, migration, Doctor, update, service-lifecycle, or plugin-loading path. Older versions ignore unknown plugin-state keys; an empty candidate cache repopulates. A separate published-driver × candidate update-proof cell does not apply to this PR.

The supplemental core-tarball probe retained the published external Codex plugin because the ordinary core package excludes it. Its empty-snapshot assertion therefore did not exercise C3 and is an artifact-selection gap, not an established candidate defect. That proof work was stopped and all owned leases were closed. The coordinator-approved full-scope review and the fresh bounded review are clean at P2; older discovery, the shared scan allowance, and logical backoff settlement are covered by the recorded regressions.
